terms.gloss: a group, a set, a circle of people
evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.9.13: scrībe tuī gregis hunc
terms.comment: Properly a flock; of people, a company or set, in a good or bad sense (Lewis & Short): a circle of friends, a school of philosophers, or a gang (in hunc gregem, Cic. Sull. 77). In groups: gregātim.

terms.gloss: a crowd, a band of people
evidence: Cic. Mur. 69: cum bene magnā catervā suā (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: a circle of people talking together
evidence: Cic. Balb. 57: in convīviīs rōdunt, in circulīs vellicant (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: a knot, a throng of people

phrases.latin: scrībe tuī gregis hunc et fortem crēde bonumque
phrases.english: count him one of your circle, and believe him brave and good
elephants always move about in groups

sources: Lewis & Short: grex · Lewis & Short: caterva · Lewis & Short: circulus · Lewis & Short: globus · Lewis & Short: gregatim
